clue.text: Trollope's churchman is haughty, that is to say

parts.note: a bishop is a senior churchman
haughty means proud
i.e. (id est) is Latin shorthand for 'that is to say'

explanation.surface: A Trollope clergyman is described as arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barchester novels of Anthony Trollope feature the henpecked bishop of that name; the clue's 'Trollope's' stands for his character. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's Barchester novels feature this bishop as a leading clerical character.

clue.text: Small change from Coleridge

parts.note: small change is a pile of low-value coins; the phrase is also a title linked with Coleridge

explanation.surface: Some loose coins handed over by the poet Coleridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Farthings were the smallest old British coins, so a sack of them is literally small change.

clue.text: Dreadful toils of a maestro

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something mangled or wrecked, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor's terrible labours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' is a link. Georg Solti was a famous Hungarian-British conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a celebrated orchestral conductor, a maestro.

clue.text: Reading inspired him to write a ballad

definitions.text: Reading inspired him to write a ballad

parts.words: Reading inspired him to write a ballad
parts.note: Reading looks like the act of reading books but is the English town whose gaol held the writer

explanation.surface: Books he read prompted a writer to compose a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is the town, not the pastime: imprisoned in Reading Gaol, he wrote 'The Ballad of Reading Gaol'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright was jailed in Reading and afterwards wrote the famous ballad about it.

clue.text: His mummy outlived him

parts.note: mummy reads as a mother but means an embalmed body that survives for millennia

explanation.surface: A man's mother survived him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' reads as his mother, but means his embalmed corpse, which has lasted thousands of years.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptian kings were embalmed, and their preserved bodies survive today.

clue.text: She was described as being "of a holy, cold, and still conversation"

definitions.text: She was described as being "of a holy, cold, and still conversation"

parts.words: She was described as being "of a holy, cold, and still conversation"
parts.note: the quotation is Enobarbus describing Caesar's sister, Antony's wife, in Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A woman characterised by quotation as chaste and reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Enobarbus speaks these words about Antony's Roman wife, sister of Octavius Caesar.

clue.text: One who wrote by request

parts.note: 'By Request' is the title of a 1927 novel by the popular romance writer Ethel M.

explanation.surface: A writer who produced work on commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by request' looks like writing to order, but 'By Request' is a title by Ethel M. Dell, the popular romantic novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel M. Dell, a bestselling romance novelist, published a book titled 'By Request'.

clue.text: Charmed by island, in spite of noise we hear

definitions.text: Charmed by island, in spite of noise we hear

parts.words: Charmed by island, in spite of noise we hear
parts.note: recalls The Tempest, where Caliban's isle is full of noises yet spellbound by Prospero's magic

explanation.surface: Someone delighted by an island despite its din.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero's isle in The Tempest is under a spell, and Caliban says it is 'full of noises'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed means under a spell, as Prospero's magic island is in The Tempest.

clue.text: Mann portraying inhumanity to man with leading practitioner of 16

definitions.text: Mann portraying inhumanity to man with leading practitioner of 16

parts.words: Mann portraying inhumanity to man with leading practitioner of 16
parts.note: Klaus Mann's novel Mephisto portrays a man who sells out to evil; the chief practitioner of devilry (16) is the Faustian devil

explanation.surface: A German novelist depicting cruelty through a figure skilled in the dark arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is DIABOLISM; its leading practitioner is Faust's tempter, whose short name titles Klaus Mann's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil to whom Faust sells his soul is the archetypal servant of Satan, a master of devilry.

clue.text: Leonard's riches move steadily on

parts.note: gold stands for wealth or riches
to coast is to move along without effort, under momentum

explanation.surface: A wealthy man keeps rolling forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leonard's' is the definition: Elmore Leonard wrote a crime novel of this title, set in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmore Leonard's 1980 crime thriller carries this title.

clue.text: Did this English physician, "Father of Classical Liberalism", provide a key to his work?

definitions.text: Did this English physician, "Father of Classical Liberalism", provide a key to his work?

parts.words: Did this English physician, "Father of Classical Liberalism", provide a key to his work?
parts.note: the philosopher trained as a physician; his surname sounds like a fastening that a key opens

explanation.surface: Asks whether a doctor-philosopher supplied a guide to his own writings.
explanation.walkthrough: John Locke trained in medicine; a key fits a lock, which is the joke on his name.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke, physician and philosopher, is called the father of classical liberalism.

clue.text: As Laurence, his assistance was fatally unhelpful

definitions.text: As Laurence, his assistance was fatally unhelpful

parts.words: As Laurence, his assistance was fatally unhelpful
parts.note: in Romeo and Juliet the cleric Laurence supplies the sleeping potion whose plan ends in both lovers' deaths

explanation.surface: A man named Laurence whose help proved deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence in Romeo and Juliet is a Franciscan monk whose scheme goes tragically wrong.

clue.text: Duke known to the Dutch as 21

definitions.text: Duke known to the Dutch as 21

parts.words: Duke known to the Dutch as 21
parts.note: 21 is IRON: the Spanish governor of the Netherlands was nicknamed the Iron Duke by the Dutch

explanation.surface: A nobleman with a Dutch nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish duke who ruled the Netherlands harshly was called the Iron Duke there.

clue.text: He wrote many long years ago

definitions.text: He wrote many long years ago

parts.words: He wrote many long years ago
parts.note: the Elizabethan pamphleteer Thomas wrote prolifically centuries back

explanation.surface: An author was prolific in the distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nash(e) was a prolific Elizabethan writer of pamphlets and satire.

clue.text: Kennedy bestseller, sure way to rapid enrichment

explanation.surface: A popular book is a guaranteed route to wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Kennedy's 1938 novel has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Kennedy wrote a novel of this name; and King Midas turned all he touched to gold, a byword for instant riches.

clue.text: Identity of this poet recognizable in Ronald Richards

indicators.note: the poet can be recognised sitting inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A poet's identity can be spotted in someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Bailey Aldrich was an American poet and editor. 'Identity of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Bailey Aldrich was a nineteenth-century American poet.

clue.text: The Devil's Mode of Burgess, perhaps, leaving all in his Devil of a State

definitions.text: The Devil's Mode of Burgess, perhaps, leaving all in his Devil of a State

parts.words: The Devil's Mode of Burgess, perhaps, leaving all in his Devil of a State
parts.note: Anthony Burgess wrote 'The Devil's Mode' and 'Devil of a State'; the devil's mode of conduct is worship of evil

explanation.surface: Wordplay on two Anthony Burgess titles about the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil worship or sorcery is the devil's way of operating.

clue.text: How Francis gets to a finish?

definitions.text: How Francis gets to a finish?

parts.words: How Francis gets to a finish?
parts.note: Sir Francis Chichester the aviator reached his destinations by flying

explanation.surface: Asks how someone called Francis reaches the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Chichester was a pioneer pilot, so he flies to his destination.

clue.text: Mad sort of mad sort in powerful position

indicators.note: a mad sort of version of the following words means their letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A deranged person in a seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad sort of' signals the anagram of MADSORT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule of a Russian emperor was a position of absolute power.

clue.text: "Age seeketh rather a — for sustenance, than feastes for Surfets" (Lyly, Euphues)

parts.note: the gap wants a word meaning a small amount, set against feasts

explanation.surface: A quotation from Lyly's Euphues with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quantity of food, enough to live on, contrasted with gluttonous feasts.

clue.text: A bravo for Chilean art

parts.note: bravo looks like applause but is the surname of a hyperrealist painter from Chile

explanation.surface: Applause for the art of Chile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bravo' is not applause: Claudio Bravo was a Chilean painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Bravo was a celebrated Chilean realist painter.

clue.text: Thriller writer who raised a massive subject

definitions.text: Thriller writer who raised a massive subject

parts.words: Thriller writer who raised a massive subject
parts.note: the American thriller writer Clive wrote 'Raise the Titanic!', about lifting a huge liner

explanation.surface: A novelist who brought up a weighty topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised a massive subject' looks like broaching a big topic; it is 'Raise the Titanic!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive Cussler wrote the thriller 'Raise the Titanic!'.

clue.text: Press club

explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes flat uses a smoothing appliance; a golf club with an angled metal head shares the name.

clue.text: First of Dryden's early significant poems

indicators.note: the first letters of the four following words are taken

explanation.surface: The earliest of Dryden's important poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like 'first of Dryden's', but it takes the initial of 'of' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, a form Dryden wrote.

clue.text: Five books in five letters

parts.note: the five books of Moses have a Hebrew name spelt with five letters

explanation.surface: Five volumes squeezed into five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentateuch, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, has this five-letter Hebrew name.

clue.text: King discreetly assassinated, leaving him red-faced

definitions.text: King discreetly assassinated, leaving him red-faced

parts.words: King discreetly assassinated, leaving him red-faced
parts.note: William II died in a hunting 'accident'; his Latin nickname means red

explanation.surface: A monarch quietly killed and left embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red-faced' looks like shame, but William II's nickname, Latin for red, refers to his ruddy face; he was shot in the New Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: William II of England, killed by an arrow while hunting, was nicknamed for his ruddy complexion.

clue.text: Direction of American novelist making a cool million

definitions.text: American novelist making a cool million

explanation.surface: A compass point for a writer who earns big money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Cool Million' is a novel by Nathanael West.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point opposite east; and Nathanael West, the American author of 'A Cool Million'.

clue.text: Narayan's showed the way

explanation.definitionFit: R. K. Narayan's novel is titled after its hero, who leads tourists and later disciples.

parts.note: the gap wants an adjective meaning vivid and eventful

parts.words: Some fundamental changes made in Rome
parts.note: Ovid, a Roman poet, wrote a poem of tales of transformations

explanation.surface: Radical reforms carried out in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes made in Rome' looks like politics; it is Ovid's poem of transformations.
